excerpt_i18n.en: At the opening of ISC.AI 2026 (the 14th Internet Security Conference) today, Zhou Hongyi, founder of 360 Group, officially unveiled two core capabilities of 360 AI Security, named "Yitu Long" and "Yitian Zhen": the vulnerability automated mining agent "Tulong Feng" and the network security automated defense system "Yitian Zhen." Meanwhile, 360, together with industry partners including Feiteng, Kylin, and others in the fields of information technology application innovation, security, cloud computing, large models, and computing power, jointly launched the "Rock Shield" security collaboration initiative. Recently, Anthropic announced restrictions on the public access to its most powerful internal model, Mythos, drawing widespread attention from the global security industry. Early in the model's debut, it triggered a collective plunge in the stock prices of major U.S. cybersecurity giants. Zhou Hongyi believes that the fundamental reason Mythos caused such a stir is its ability to autonomously discover vulnerabilities, analyze them, and even construct cyberattack "weapons," essentially acting as a "cyber nuclear weapon" in the AI era, creating a new form of strategic deterrence. Over the past 30 years, the balance of cyber offense and defense has largely relied on the difficulty of finding vulnerabilities. High-value vulnerabilities are limited in number and costly to discover, often only within the reach of a few top security experts and national-level teams with sustained mining capabilities. However, AI is changing all of this. It makes vulnerability discovery faster, cheaper, and more scalable, replicating capabilities once held by a select few. A large number of long-dormant, hard-to-find legacy vulnerabilities will be unearthed one after another. When vulnerabilities shift from scarce resources to scalable ones, the rules of the cybersecurity industry, which have governed for 30 years, will be completely rewritten.
excerpt_i18n.es: En la inauguración hoy de la ISC.AI 2026 (14ª Conferencia de Seguridad en Internet), Zhou Hongyi, fundador de 360 Group, presentó oficialmente las dos capacidades principales de seguridad de IA de 360, "Yitian Tulong": el agente de automatización de detección de vulnerabilidades "Tulongfeng" y el sistema de defensa automatizado de seguridad de redes "Yitianzhen". Al mismo tiempo, 360, junto con socios industriales como Feiteng y Qilin en los ámbitos de innovación tecnológica, seguridad, computación en la nube, grandes modelos y potencia de cálculo, lanzaron conjuntamente el plan de colaboración de seguridad "Escudo de Roca". Recientemente, Anthropic anunció la restricción del acceso público a su modelo interno más potente, Mythos, lo que ha generado una amplia preocupación en la industria de seguridad global. Ya en las primeras etapas de la aparición de este modelo, provocó una serie de reacciones en la comunidad de redes de Estados Unidos.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Lei Feng exclusively learned that Qingyan Precision, a Tsinghua-incubated physical AI company, has recently completed a B3 funding round of several hundred million yuan. This round was led by the Beijing Green Energy Fund and BAIC Capital, with Yulon Group participating as a follow-on investor. The funds will be used for core talent recruitment, R&D and large-scale deployment of multimodal data acquisition equipment, as well as computing power procurement and model training infrastructure construction.  

01 Tsinghua-incubated, spanning multiple fields including automotive  
Founded in 2018 and incubated by Tsinghua University, Qingyan Precision is dedicated to building an engineering foundation for physical AI. The founder and CEO, Dong Han, holds a Ph.D. from Tsinghua University and studied under Professor Li Keqiang, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. He has nearly a decade of research and industry experience in the automotive sector. The Director of Strategic Development and CEO of Precision Vision, Cao Qitong, holds a Master’s degree in Management Science and Engineering from Stanford University and a Bachelor’s degree in Applied Mathematics from Duke University. The core research team and collaborators come from top universities such as Tsinghua, Stanford, Zhejiang University, Beihang University, and Xi’an Jiaotong University. They integrate autonomous driving engineering with interdisciplinary computing capabilities, adapting to core business areas such as industrial multimodal perception and physical simulation under complex working conditions, providing technical support for industrial-grade applications.  

Currently, Qingyan Precision has integrated its AI inspection, simulation, and testing verification products into the core supply chains of over 100 domestic OEMs, as well as power battery and energy storage companies. Its customers span automotive, new energy, engineering machinery, and low-altitude economy sectors.
